# routeros_ip_cloud_back_to_home_user (Resource)


## Example Usage
```terraform
resource "routeros_ip_cloud_back_to_home_user" "user" {
  name      = "example"
  allow_lan = true
  comment   = "Managed by OpenTofu"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Informative name of the Back To Home user.

### Optional

- `___id___` (Number) <em>Resource ID type (.id / name). This is an internal service field, setting a value is not required.</em>
- `___path___` (String) <em>Resource path for CRUD operations. This is an internal service field, setting a value is not required.</em>
- `allow_lan` (Boolean) Allows the user to reach the local network behind the router. When it is disabled the user is added to a firewall address list that only permits internet access.
- `comment` (String)
- `disabled` (Boolean)
- `expires` (String) Expiration time and date of the user, `never` or an ISO 8601 `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` value. MikroTik documents that it cannot be changed once the user has been created, so the resource is recreated when this attribute changes.
- `file_access` (String) Level of access the user gets to the directory given by `file_access_path`.
  * disabled - no file access at all.
  * read-only - the user may browse and download.
  * full - the user may also upload and delete.
- `file_access_path` (String) Directory on the router the user is allowed to browse. Using the router root (`/`) is not recommended: a user with full access to it can delete system files or upload malicious `.npk` packages.
- `private_key` (String, Sensitive) WireGuard private key of the user. If it is not set manually, it is generated by the system.
- `public_key` (String) WireGuard public key of the user. If it is not set manually, it is generated by the system.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.

## Import
Import is supported using the following syntax:
```shell
#The ID can be found via API or the terminal
#The command for the terminal is -> :put [/ip/cloud/back-to-home-user get [print show-ids]]
terraform import routeros_ip_cloud_back_to_home_user.user "*1"
```
